{{Quote|The legends of my homeworld of Irmenu speak of the great mariner Darakaer, who sleeps until the faithful summon him by drumming out their call for help. When Gilad and I parted long ago, we reminded each other of that story, and we pledged that each of us would answer Darakaer's rhythm if the other should be in need.|Natasi Daala|<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
[[Irmenu]] was an [[Ocean/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the fringes of the [[Crombach Nebula/Legends|Crombach Nebula]], in the [[Belsmuth sector/Legends|Belsmuth sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Isolated from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]], it was a feudal world known for its seafaring and stern religious traditions.<ref name="ZotR" />

==Description==
{{Quote|He's just drowning in the war like everyone else, grabbing what flotsam he can to stay afloat.''"<br />"''You're in full Imperial Irmenu Navy mode today, I see.''"<br />"''It's the water. Brings out my inner sailor.|[[Kal Skirata]] and Walon Vau|<ref name="Order 66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
Irmenu's location in the hazardous [[Crombach Nebula/Legends|Crombach Nebula]] contributed to its isolation from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It was an [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]]-[[Waterworld/Legends|covered]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with a single submerged continental shelf covering half its surface. The continental shelf was mostly covered with shallow seas, with the highest points reaching above the water to form island archipelagos. These islands ranged from sandy spits of land to crags of rock that could reach hundreds of [[Meter/Legends|meters]] into the [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]], topped by [[Tree/Legends|forests]] and [[Grass/Legends|meadowlands]].<ref name="ZotR" />

Irmenu had a single large [[Moon/Legends|moon]] that followed an eccentric [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. Consequently, the planet had dramatic and complex tides. Away from the continental shelf, Irmenu's oceans were deep and stormy and had numerous abyssal trenches.<ref name="ZotR" />

==History==
{{Quote|It's just that they don't seem to understand ''why'' I took certain actions. They make me sound like a criminal. They're only saying what I hear crew whispering in the mess&mdash;saying that I've killed a lot of people, and that I wasn't on duty when Mara Skywalker was killed, and that they wouldn't put it past me to assassinate even my own aunt&mdash;like one of those lunatic inbred Irmenu emperors.|[[Darth Caedus]], to [[Lon Shevu]]|<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>}}
Irmenu was one of the galaxy's many lost [[Colonist/Legends|colonies]]; the circumstances of its founding by [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists were shrouded in mystery. An [[Emperor/Legends|emperor]] ruled Irmenu [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], but the tyrannical imperial family was overthrown by the [[Irmenu (people)|Irmenu]] [[Noble/Legends|aristocracy]] several centuries before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], leaving the [[Irmenu imperial palace|imperial palace]] in ruins.<ref name="ZotR" />

The planet was rediscovered by the galaxy several centuries before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which led to increased [[Merchant/Legends|trade]], as well as the offworld [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] of those Irmenu that had fallen afoul of the [[Imperius]] [[Priest/Legends|priesthood]]. Tales told by these exiles made Irmenu an object of curiosity in the wider galaxy. Notable exiles included [[Walon Vau]], the son of [[Walon Vau's father|the]] [[Count of Gesl]] who was exiled after a doomed love affair with the [[Prince/Legends|princess]] of a neighboring province. He later became a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] and a member of the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]''. Another such exile was [[Natasi Daala]], who grew up on [[Botajef/Legends|Botajef]] but later discovered that she was an Irmenu princess from a family whose holdings had been overrun and seized by rivals. The rest of Daala's family had been put to [[Death/Legends|death]], but a younger son of the victorious family took pity on the baby and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggled]] her offworld, leaving her as a foundling at a Botajef orphanage.<ref name="ZotR" />

Around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Irmenu had a population of some 5 million Humans.<ref name="ZotR" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Thanks for saving my life. And I'm sorry that it cost one of your men.''"<br />"''That's the job, ma'am. You understand that as well as anybody.''"<br />"''Never be a prisoner and never take one. That's what the Irmenu say.|[[Hallena Devis]] and [[Rex/Legends|Rex]]|<ref name="TCW:NP">''[[The Clone Wars: No Prisoners]]''</ref>}}
A feudal, caste-based society, the Irmenu lived in kingdoms, holds and crofts and were ruled by an aristocracy of [[King/Legends|kings]], [[Duke/Legends|dukes]], [[Count/Legends|counts]], [[marquise]]s, [[Baron/Legends|barons]] and [[cavalier]]s. These nobles had near-absolute dominion over commoners bound to them by ancient [[Blood/Legends|blood]] oaths. Irmenu noblemen were known to engage in ceremonious duels.<ref name="TCW">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novelization]]</ref> Outside of this rigid social structure was the hierarchical priesthood of the Imperius, and the outcasts and excommunicates who had been exiled by them. Many of these exiles lived as [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], and were simultaneously loathed as threats to the peace and envied and romanticized for their freedom.<ref name="ZotR" />

The Irmenu were excellent [[sailor]]s, taught from birth to understand the workings of winds and tides and to [[Map/Legends|map]] the shallow seas around their home islands. [[Wood/Legends|Wooden]]-hulled [[Boat/Legends|sailing ships]] like caravels and galleons were common sights in feudal [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]]. Vendettas and wars of conquest between fiefs were common, and Irmenu nobles were expected to be good naval [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] and [[Commander/Legends|commanders]]. The Imperius prevented feuds from spiraling out of control with the threat of spiritual censure, which could be as extreme as excommunication and exile. The Imperius also operated the [[Imperial Irmenu Navy]], which patrolled the seas, rescued sailors in distress, and fought pirates; tours of duty in the [[Navy/Legends|navy]] were a religious obligation for members of the aristocracy. Second sons who would not inherit wealth or a title would often go into its permanent service.<ref name="ZotR" /> Ancient Irmenu military doctrine had it that [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] of war were both burdens to their captors and liabilities to their own side, and warned against either taking prisoners or surrendering. Rumor had it that this doctrine continued to by practiced as late as the Clone Wars.<ref name="TCW:NP" />

Irmenu maintained contact with the greater galaxy via a single [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] run by the Imperius, which had allowed some technology like [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and [[Comlink/Legends|comlinks]] to reach the planet. These formed somewhat incongruous sights when used aboard ancient wooden-hulled caravels and galleons flying heraldic banners. The [[Count/Legends|Counts]] of [[Gesl]] even maintained a [[Bank/Legends|bank]] vault in the [[Dressian Kiolsh Merchant Bank]] on [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]] to store their fortune.<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> However, both the Imperius and the Irmenu themselves were ambivalent about such contact. One benefit of contact, however, was that Irmenu who ran afoul of their society's mores could be exiled to other worlds instead of to inhospitable islands.<ref name="ZotR" />

The Irmenu had a story of a warrior-sailor known as [[Darakaer]] in their folklore. It was said that he would come to their aid should they ever need it if they summoned him by beating his ancient [[Drum/Legends|drum]]. Natasi Daala was inspired by the story to create a coded signal she gave to [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] to use should he ever need to summon her after her self-imposed exile from the galaxy at large in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Don't damage that boat, Walon.''"<br />"''Ah, you're learning. It is indeed a boat in this mode. Not a ship.''"<br />"''When did you get to be such a stickler for naval terminology?''"<br />"''My father was an admiral in the Imperial Irmenu Navy.|[[Kal Skirata]] and Walon Vau|<ref name="TC" />}}
Irmenu was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] in the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novel [[Republic Commando: True Colors|''True Colors'']], written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published on [[October 30]], [[2007]].<ref name="TC" /> Subsequently, the planet went on to receive mentions and references in a number of other Traviss works, including ''True Colors''<nowiki>'</nowiki> sequels, [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']]<ref name="Order 66" /> and ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]'',<ref name="IC">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref> the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novel [[Legacy of the Force: Revelation|''Revelation'']],<ref name="Revelation" /> and her two ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' tie-in novels, the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|film novelization]]<ref name="TCW" /> and [[The Clone Wars: No Prisoners|''No Prisoners'']].<ref name="TCW:NP" />

Irmenu received a brief mention in ''Star Wars'' reference guidebook ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', co-authored by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]], and published on [[April 3]], [[2012]].<ref name="TEGtW" /> The world was originally set to feature more prominently in the book, but a section on Irmenu was cut from the final draft,<ref name="Endnotes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/27417920547/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-16|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 16}}</ref> only to later feature in the fifth installment of Jason Fry's official [[Star Wars Blog|''Star Wars'' Blog]] series, ''[[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut]]''.<ref name="ZotR" />
